thread:
elaine: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a refactor to the trace joiner to use sliding windows + watermarking. late spans are creating duplicate cost attribution across adjacent windows. can we sync briefly?
raj: ack. can you sketch the failure mode? is this only from out-of-order spans or also partial flushes from collectors? :thinking:
elaine: mostly out-of-order + clients that flush a partial trace after a retry. current windowing is fixed tumbling 1m buckets; a span that arrives 70s late ends up being counted in both windows during stitch.
miguel: ouch. that explains the cost bump we saw in eu-prod last week. saw a ~7% increase in billed events where trace_id existed in two windows.
sara: is the plan to move to sliding windows or to add a dedupe/merge step after join? both have tradeoffs.
elaine: want sliding window with watermark + idempotent trace anchors. idea: keep a lightweight trace anchor record with last-seen timestamp & cost-sum that downstream joiner consults. windows overlap by 30s; watermark advances at 15s behind event-time. duplicates are suppressed using trace anchor versioning.
raj: sounds reasonable. two concerns: 1) anchors add storage/touch on the critical path (latency), 2) watermark lag affects end-to-end attribution freshness.
miguel: storage can be bounded by TTL and sharded hot cache. we could store anchors in a local memtable + async durable log. on misses, joiner falls back to best-effort.
sara: rollout idea: dark mirror the sliding-window joiner for one region (us-west) and compare metrics for 72h. key metrics: duplicate_trace_count, avg_attribution_lag, billed_event_rate_delta, join_latency_p50/95. create alert if duplicate_trace_count > baseline+1%.
elaine: agreed. also plan to expose a per-trace debug flag to force full rejoin for a trace_id if we detect mismatch. that'll help post-mortems.
raj: implement detail: watermark watermark_delay = 15s; sliding_window_size = 90s; slide_step = 30s. pseudoconfig: ```yaml
joiner:
  mode: sliding
  window_size_seconds: 90
  slide_seconds: 30
  watermark_delay_seconds: 15
  anchor_ttl_seconds: 300
```
miguel: nice. consider adding a backoff factor to anchor writes during overload to avoid thundering writes. e.g., if kallisto-throttle hits, set anchor_ttl += 30s and write-probability down to 10%.
sara: what about analytics/queries? we must ensure billing exports remain stable and that historical aggregates don't double-count. need a migration plan for historical backfill.
elaine: for backfill we’ll run a windowed dedupe pass during off-peak. not part of the initial rollout. initial rollout only affects live attribution.
raj: ops/SRE note: we need a runbook entry for rollback. rollback = flip joiner.mode to tumbling and stop anchor writes, drain sliding instances. label config change as immediate fallback. add runbook checks for <10% traffic before draining.
sara: tests: unit for anchor races, chaos test for delayed spans (inject +-120s), and e2e perf test with 10k traces/s to validate p95 latency.
miguel: dependency callouts: instrumentation team needs to include event_time in span envelope if not already. many SDKs only set arrival_time currently.
elaine: yep — pinging @instrumentation (cc: @eng-platform). we should draft a short compatibility doc: "span.envelope.event_time required for sliding joins".
ops-bot: deployment checklist created: https://internal/redwood/boards/stream-joiner-refactor-5647 :rocket:
raj: timeline proposal: week1 feature branch + unit tests, week2 dark mirror + metrics, week3 progressive rollout to 10%/50%/100% if metrics stable. rollback gates at each stage.
sara: +1. I'll own the metrics dashboard and alerts. putting draft now in the deployment checklist.
elaine: thanks all. i'll open the follow-up PR with config and the RFC addendum. tagging this thread as followup-needed. :thumbsup:
